     3	## Source
     4	https://www.sequoiacap.com/article/generative-ai-act-two/

     6	Published September 20, 2023 by Sonya Huang, Pat Grady and GPT-4 (Sequoia Capital)
     7	
     8	## The Foundation: Decades of Convergence
     9	
    10	Generative AI's emergence is not a sudden event but the culmination of decades of technological progress:
    11	
    12	- **Six decades of Moore's Law** delivered the compute horsepower to process exaflops of data.
    13	- **Four decades of the internet** (accelerated by COVID) produced trillions of tokens of training data.
    14	- **Two decades of mobile and cloud computing** put a supercomputer in every human's palm.
    15	
    16	ChatGPT's launch was the spark that ignited a Cambrian explosion of innovation not seen since the early internet. AI researchers became rockstars, hacker houses overflowed with autonomous agents and companionship chatbots, and the arXiv printing press became so prolific that researchers jokingly called for a pause on publications.
    17	
    18	But excitement quickly turned to hysteria. Every company became an "AI copilot." Inboxes filled with undifferentiated pitches for "AI Salesforce" and "AI Adobe." The $100M pre-product seed round returned. Cracks appeared: artists challenged machine-generated IP, Washington debated regulation, and a whisper spread that generative AI was not actually useful — products fell short of expectations with terrible user retention.
    19	
    20	## Early Commercial Traction Despite Skepticism
    21	
    22	Despite the discontent, generative AI has had a more successful commercial start than SaaS, with **>$1 billion in revenue from startups alone** — a milestone that took SaaS years, not months, to reach. Standout successes include:
    23	
    24	- **ChatGPT**: Fastest-growing application in history, with strong product-market fit among students and developers.
    25	- **Midjourney**: Reported hundreds of millions of dollars in revenue with a team of just 11 people.
    26	- **Character.ai**: Popularized AI entertainment and companionship; users spend an average of **2 hours per session** in-app.
    27	
    28	However, these successes don't change the reality that many AI companies lack product-market fit or sustainable competitive advantage.
    29	
    30	## The Retention Problem: AI-First Apps vs. Incumbents
    31	
    32	Mobile app retention data reveals a stark gap between established consumer apps and AI-first companies:
    33

    56	
    57	A separate monthly active usage benchmark for incumbents shows even higher engagement bars:
    58

    60	|---|---|
    61	| YouTube | 85% |

    73	
    74	## From Act 1 to Act 2
    75	
    76	Sequoia frames the generative AI market as transitioning between two phases:
    77	
    78	**Act 1 (Technology-Out):** The discovery of foundation models as a new "hammer" led to a wave of novelty apps — lightweight demonstrations of cool technology. These apps used foundation models as the entire solution and often lacked stickiness.
    79	
    80	**Act 2 (Customer-Back):** The emerging phase focuses on solving human problems end-to-end. Key characteristics of Act 2 companies:
    81	
    82	- Use foundation models as **a piece** of a more comprehensive solution, not the entire product
    83	- Introduce **new editing interfaces** that make workflows stickier and outputs better
    84	- Are often **multi-modal** in nature
    85	- Solve problems **end-to-end** rather than offering thin wrappers
    86	
    87	Examples of Act 2 companies: **Harvey** (custom LLMs for elite law firms), **Glean** (crawling and indexing workspaces for relevant enterprise AI), **Character** and **Ava** (digital companions).
    88	
    89	The updated Sequoia generative AI market map is now organized **by use case rather than model modality**, reflecting the evolution from technology hammer to actual value delivery and the increasingly multi-modal nature of applications.
    90	
    91	## Key Findings
    92	
    93	- **Generative AI startups exceeded $1B in revenue faster than SaaS**, proving real commercial demand despite hype-cycle skepticism.
    94	- **AI-first apps face a severe retention gap**: 14% median retention vs. 51% for incumbent consumer apps — a 3.6x disadvantage.
    95	- **The market is shifting from Act 1 (technology-out) to Act 2 (customer-back)**, where foundation models become components of comprehensive, workflow-integrated solutions rather than standalone products.
    96	- **Multi-modal, end-to-end problem solving** and new editing interfaces are the hallmarks of companies likely to win in Act 2.
    97	- **Character.ai is the retention outlier** among AI-first apps at 41%, approaching incumbent levels, suggesting that companionship/entertainment may be generative AI's strongest consumer use case.

    11	## When to Use
    12	
    13	Use when the main artifact is a Microsoft PowerPoint presentation or `.pptx` deck, especially when layouts, templates, placeholders, notes, comments, charts, extraction, editing, or final visual quality matter.
    14	
    15	## Core Rules
    16	
    17	### 1. Choose the workflow before touching the deck
    18	
    19	- Reading text, editing an existing deck, rebuilding from a template, and creating from scratch are different jobs with different failure modes.
    20	- For text extraction or inspection, read the deck before editing it.
    21	- Text extraction plus thumbnail-style visual inspection is safer than editing from shape assumptions alone.
    22	- For template-driven work, inventory the deck before replacing content.
    23	- For deep edits, remember a `.pptx` file is OOXML with separate parts for slides, layouts, masters, media, notes, and comments.
    24	- If a template exists, template fidelity beats generic slide-design instincts.
    25	- Reusing or duplicating a good existing slide is often safer than rebuilding it and hoping the theme still matches.
    26	
    27	### 2. Inventory the deck before replacing content
    28	
    29	- Count the reusable layouts, real placeholders, notes, comments, media, and recurring typography or color patterns first.
    30	- Placeholder indexes and layout indexes are not portable assumptions.
    31	- Inspect the actual slide or template before targeting title, body, chart, or image shapes.
    32	- Speaker notes, comments, and linked assets can live outside the visible slide surface.
    33	- A missing or wrong placeholder target can silently land content in the wrong box or wrong layer.
    34	- Master and layout settings can override local slide edits, so the visible problem is not always on the slide you are editing.
    35	
    36	### 3. Match content to the actual placeholders
    37	
    38	- Count the actual content pieces before choosing a layout.
    39	- Pick layouts based on the real number of ideas, columns, images, or charts the slide needs.
    40	- Do not force two ideas into a three-column slide or cram dense text under a chart.
    41	- Category counts and data series lengths must match or charts will break in ugly ways.
    42	- Explicit sizing beats wishful thinking: text boxes, images, and charts need real space, not "it should fit".
    43	- Do not choose a layout with more placeholders than the content can meaningfully fill.
    44	- Quote layouts are for real quotes, and image-led layouts are for slides that actually have images.
    45	- For chart-, table-, or image-heavy slides, full-slide or two-column layouts are usually safer than stacking dense text above the visual.
    46	
    47	### 4. Preserve the deck's visual language
    48	
    49	- Theme, master, and layout files usually decide fonts, colors, and hierarchy more than any one slide does.
    50	- Start from the deck's actual theme, fonts, spacing, and aspect ratio instead of improvising a new style.
    51	- Reuse the deck's own alignment and spacing system instead of inventing a second visual language.
    52	- Use common fonts for portability and strong contrast for readability.
    53	- Preserve the template's visual logic first; originality matters less than not breaking the deck's existing language.
    54	- Combining slides from multiple sources requires normalizing themes, masters, and alignment afterward.
    55	
    56	### 5. Run content QA and visual QA separately
    57	
    58	- Text overflow, bad alignment, clipped shapes, weak contrast, and placeholder leftovers are normal first-pass failures.
    59	- Run both content QA and visual QA; missing text and broken layout are different failure classes.
    60	- Render or inspect the actual deck output before delivery when layout matters.
    61	- Search for leftover template junk, sample labels, and placeholder text before calling the deck finished.
    62	- Check notes, comments, labels, legends, and chart/table semantics separately from the visual pass.
    63	- A deck can pass text extraction and still fail on overlap, clipping, wrong theme inheritance, or broken notes.
    64	- Thumbnail grids and rendered slides usually reveal layout bugs faster than code or text inspection.
    65	- Assume the first render is wrong and do at least one fix-and-verify cycle before calling the deck finished.
    66	- Re-check affected slides after each fix because one spacing change often creates another issue.
    67	
    68	### 6. Keep decks portable and review-safe
    69	
    70	- Template masters can override direct edits in surprising ways.
    71	- Complex effects may degrade across PowerPoint, LibreOffice, and conversion pipelines, so keep important content robust without them.
    72	- Image sizing, font substitution, and placeholder mismatch are common reasons a deck looks good in code and bad on screen.
    73	- Notes, comments, linked media, and merged decks can stay broken even when the visible slide looks fine.
    74	
    75	## Common Traps
    76	
    77	- Placeholder text and sample charts often survive template reuse if not explicitly replaced.
    78	- Directly editing one slide can fail if the real issue lives in the master or layout.
    79	- Charts, icons, and text boxes need enough space; near-collisions are usually visible only after rendering.
    80	- Layout indexes vary by template, so built-in assumptions from one deck often break in another.
    81	- A missing placeholder or wrong shape target can silently put content in the wrong place.
    82	- Counting the text ideas after choosing the layout usually leads to empty placeholders, weak hierarchy, or leftover template junk.
    83	- Font substitution can move line breaks and wreck careful spacing.
    84	- Speaker notes, comments, and linked media can stay broken even when the visible slide looks fine.
    85	- A deck can pass text inspection and still fail visually because of overlap, contrast, or edge clipping.
    86	- Editing from one slide alone can miss the real source of truth in the theme, master, or layout definitions.
    87	- Choosing a quote, comparison, or multi-column layout without matching content usually makes the deck look templated rather than intentional.
    88	- Combining or duplicating slides without checking masters and themes can create subtle inconsistency slide by slide.
    89	- Aspect-ratio mismatches like `16:9` versus `4:3` can shift every placement decision even when each slide looks locally reasonable.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Build the 8-slide Sequoia Capital GenAI Act Two presentation.
Uses python-pptx with a clean, data-forward, analytical design.
"""

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.dml.color import RgbColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.oxml.ns import nsmap
from pptx.oxml import parse_xml
from lxml import etree
import copy

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constants
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SLIDE_WIDTH = Inches(13.333)
SLIDE_HEIGHT = Inches(7.5)

# Sequoia-inspired palette
COLOR_BG = RgbColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
COLOR_DARK = RgbColor(0x1A, 0x1A, 0x1A)
COLOR_TEXT = RgbColor(0x33, 0x33, 0x33)
COLOR_TEXT_LIGHT = RgbColor(0x66, 0x66, 0x66)
COLOR_ACCENT = RgbColor(0xC4, 0x1E, 0x3A)  # Sequoia red
COLOR_ACCENT_DARK = RgbColor(0x8B, 0x15, 0x28)
COLOR_SECONDARY = RgbColor(0x2E, 0x4A, 0x3F)  # deep green
COLOR_CHART_INCUMBENT = RgbColor(0x2E, 0x4A, 0x3F)
COLOR_CHART_AIFIRST = RgbColor(0xC4, 0x1E, 0x3A)
COLOR_MEDIAN_LINE = RgbColor(0x88, 0x88, 0x88)

FONT_HEADING = "Calibri Light"
FONT_BODY = "Calibri"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def set_slide_bg(slide, color=COLOR_BG):
    background = slide.background
    fill = background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color


def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size, font_name=FONT_BODY,
                bold=False, color=COLOR_TEXT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, valign=MSO_ANCHOR.TOP):
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = font_size
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.color.rgb = color
    p.alignment = align
    tf.paragraphs[0].space_after = Pt(0)
    tf.paragraphs[0].space_before = Pt(0)
    return tf


def add_bullet_list(slide, left, top, width, height, items, font_size=Pt(16),
                    color=COLOR_TEXT, bullet_color=COLOR_ACCENT, line_spacing=1.3):
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, item in enumerate(items):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = item
        p.font.size = font_size
        p.font.name = FONT_BODY
        p.font.color.rgb = color
        p.level = 0
        p.space_after = Pt(10)
        p.line_spacing = line_spacing
        # bullet via font character
        p.text = "•  " + item
    return tf


def add_shape_line(slide, left, top, width, height, color, thickness=Pt(1)):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.fill.background()
    shape.line.color.rgb = color
    shape.line.width = thickness
    return shape


def add_accent_bar(slide, left=Inches(0), top=Inches(0), width=Inches(0.15), height=Inches(7.5)):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT
    shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape


def set_text_frame_margins(tf, margin_left=Pt(6), margin_right=Pt(6), margin_top=Pt(6), margin_bottom=Pt(6)):
    # python-pptx doesn't expose margins directly; we rely on internal xml
    bodyPr = tf._bodyPr
    bodyPr.set('l', str(int(margin_left)))
    bodyPr.set('r', str(int(margin_right)))
    bodyPr.set('t', str(int(margin_top)))
    bodyPr.set('b', str(int(margin_bottom)))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Slide builders
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def build_title_slide(prs):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # blank
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    set_slide_bg(slide)

    # accent bar left
    add_accent_bar(slide, left=Inches(0), top=Inches(0), width=Inches(0.18), height=Inches(7.5))

    # small attribution top
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.5), Inches(12), Inches(0.4),
                "Sequoia Capital  •  September 2023",
                Pt(14), FONT_BODY, bold=False, color=COLOR_TEXT_LIGHT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    # main title
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(2.6), Inches(12), Inches(1.2),
                "Generative AI's Act Two",
                Pt(54), FONT_HEADING, bold=True, color=COLOR_DARK, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    # subtitle
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(3.7), Inches(12), Inches(0.8),
                "From Technology Hammer to Real Value",
                Pt(32), FONT_HEADING, bold=False, color=COLOR_ACCENT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    # bottom line
    add_shape_line(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(4.6), Inches(2.5), Inches(0.01), COLOR_ACCENT, Pt(3))

    # one-liner
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(5.0), Inches(11), Inches(1.0),
                "How generative AI is transitioning from novelty demos to end-to-end solutions that solve real human problems.",
                Pt(18), FONT_BODY, bold=False, color=COLOR_TEXT_LIGHT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
    return slide


def build_convergence_slide(prs):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    set_slide_bg(slide)

    # header accent bar
    add_shape_line(slide, Inches(0), Inches(0), Inches(13.333), Inches(0.08), COLOR_ACCENT, Pt(6))

    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.35), Inches(12), Inches(0.6),
                "Six Decades of Technological Progress Converged to Enable Generative AI",
                Pt(32), FONT_HEADING, bold=True, color=COLOR_DARK, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    add_shape_line(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.0), Inches(1.5), Inches(0.01), COLOR_ACCENT, Pt(2))

    # Three stacked blocks
    blocks = [
        ("6 decades", "Moore's Law", "Delivered the compute horsepower to process exaflops of data."),
        ("4 decades", "The Internet", "Produced trillions of tokens of training data — accelerated by COVID."),
        ("2 decades", "Mobile & Cloud", "Put a supercomputer in every human's palm."),
    ]
    y_start = Inches(1.4)
    h_block = Inches(1.6)
    gap = Inches(0.25)
    for i, (num, title, desc) in enumerate(blocks):
        y = y_start + i * (h_block + gap)
        # number box
        shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0.6), y, Inches(1.4), Inches(0.9))
        shape.fill.solid()
        shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT if i == 0 else (COLOR_SECONDARY if i == 1 else RgbColor(0x4A, 0x4A, 0x4A))
        shape.line.fill.background()
        tf = shape.text_frame
        tf.word_wrap = True
        p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = num
        p.font.size = Pt(20)
        p.font.bold = True
        p.font.color.rgb = RgbColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
        p.font.name = FONT_HEADING
        p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Build the 8-slide Sequoia Capital GenAI Act Two presentation.
Uses python-pptx with a clean, data-forward, analytical design.
"""

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.chart.data import ChartData
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constants
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SLIDE_WIDTH = Inches(13.333)
SLIDE_HEIGHT = Inches(7.5)

# Sequoia-inspired palette
COLOR_BG = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
COLOR_DARK = RGBColor(0x1A, 0x1A, 0x1A)
COLOR_TEXT = RGBColor(0x33, 0x33, 0x33)
COLOR_TEXT_LIGHT = RGBColor(0x66, 0x66, 0x66)
COLOR_ACCENT = RGBColor(0xC4, 0x1E, 0x3A)  # Sequoia red
COLOR_ACCENT_DARK = RGBColor(0x8B, 0x15, 0x28)
COLOR_SECONDARY = RGBColor(0x2E, 0x4A, 0x3F)  # deep green
COLOR_CHART_INCUMBENT = RGBColor(0x2E, 0x4A, 0x3F)
COLOR_CHART_AIFIRST = RGBColor(0xC4, 0x1E, 0x3A)
COLOR_MEDIAN_LINE = RGBColor(0x88, 0x88, 0x88)

FONT_HEADING = "Calibri Light"
FONT_BODY = "Calibri"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def set_slide_bg(slide, color=COLOR_BG):
    background = slide.background
    fill = background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color


def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size, font_name=FONT_BODY,
                bold=False, color=COLOR_TEXT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, valign=MSO_ANCHOR.TOP):
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = font_size
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.color.rgb = color
    p.alignment = align
    tf.paragraphs[0].space_after = Pt(0)
    tf.paragraphs[0].space_before = Pt(0)
    return tf


def add_shape_line(slide, left, top, width, height, color, thickness=Pt(1)):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.fill.background()
    shape.line.color.rgb = color
    shape.line.width = thickness
    return shape


def add_accent_bar(slide, left=Inches(0), top=Inches(0), width=Inches(0.15), height=Inches(7.5)):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT
    shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Slide builders
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def build_title_slide(prs):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # blank
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    set_slide_bg(slide)

    add_accent_bar(slide, left=Inches(0), top=Inches(0), width=Inches(0.18), height=Inches(7.5))

    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.5), Inches(12), Inches(0.4),
                "Sequoia Capital  •  September 2023",
                Pt(14), FONT_BODY, bold=False, color=COLOR_TEXT_LIGHT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(2.6), Inches(12), Inches(1.2),
                "Generative AI's Act Two",
                Pt(54), FONT_HEADING, bold=True, color=COLOR_DARK, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(3.7), Inches(12), Inches(0.8),
                "From Technology Hammer to Real Value",
                Pt(32), FONT_HEADING, bold=False, color=COLOR_ACCENT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    add_shape_line(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(4.6), Inches(2.5), Inches(0.01), COLOR_ACCENT, Pt(3))

    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(5.0), Inches(11), Inches(1.0),
                "How generative AI is transitioning from novelty demos to end-to-end solutions that solve real human problems.",
                Pt(18), FONT_BODY, bold=False, color=COLOR_TEXT_LIGHT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
    return slide


def build_convergence_slide(prs):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    set_slide_bg(slide)

    add_shape_line(slide, Inches(0), Inches(0), Inches(13.333), Inches(0.08), COLOR_ACCENT, Pt(6))

    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.35), Inches(12), Inches(0.6),
                "Six Decades of Technological Progress Converged to Enable Generative AI",
                Pt(32), FONT_HEADING, bold=True, color=COLOR_DARK, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    add_shape_line(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.0), Inches(1.5), Inches(0.01), COLOR_ACCENT, Pt(2))

    blocks = [
        ("6 decades", "Moore's Law", "Delivered the compute horsepower to process exaflops of data."),
        ("4 decades", "The Internet", "Produced trillions of tokens of training data — accelerated by COVID."),
        ("2 decades", "Mobile & Cloud", "Put a supercomputer in every human's palm."),
    ]
    y_start = Inches(1.4)
    h_block = Inches(1.6)
    gap = Inches(0.25)
    for i, (num, title, desc) in enumerate(blocks):
        y = y_start + i * (h_block + gap)
        shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0.6), y, Inches(1.4), Inches(0.9))
        shape.fill.solid()
        shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT if i == 0 else (COLOR_SECONDARY if i == 1 else RGBColor(0x4A, 0x4A, 0x4A))
        shape.line.fill.background()
        tf = shape.text_frame
        tf.word_wrap = True
        p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = num
        p.font.size = Pt(20)
        p.font.bold = True
        p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
        p.font.name = FONT_HEADING
        p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
        tf.paragraphs[0].space_after = Pt(0)
        add_textbox(slide, Inches(2.2), y, Inches(10), Inches(0.5), title, Pt(24), FONT_HEADING, bold=True, color=COLOR_DARK)
        add_textbox(slide, Inches(2.2), y + Inches(0.45), Inches(10), Inches(0.8), desc, Pt(18), FONT_BODY, color=COLOR_TEXT)

    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(6.1), Inches(12), Inches(0.8),
                "ChatGPT's launch ignited a Cambrian explosion of innovation — but excitement quickly turned to hysteria, revealing cracks in product-market fit and retention.",
                Pt(16), FONT_BODY, color=COLOR_TEXT_LIGHT)
    return slide


def build_traction_slide(prs):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    set_slide_bg(slide)

    add_shape_line(slide, Inches(0), Inches(0), Inches(13.333), Inches(0.08), COLOR_ACCENT, Pt(6))

    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.35), Inches(12), Inches(0.6),
                "GenAI Startups Surpassed $1B Revenue Faster Than SaaS Ever Did",
                Pt(32), FONT_HEADING, bold=True, color=COLOR_DARK, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
    add_shape_line(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.0), Inches(1.5), Inches(0.01), COLOR_ACCENT, Pt(2))

    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.3), Inches(5.5), Inches(1.0),
                ">$1B", Pt(60), FONT_HEADING, bold=True, color=COLOR_ACCENT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(2.15), Inches(5.5), Inches(0.5),
                "in startup revenue in months — a milestone that took SaaS years.",
                Pt(18), FONT_BODY, color=COLOR_TEXT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    cards = [
        ("ChatGPT", "Fastest-growing application in history, with strong product-market fit among students and developers."),
        ("Midjourney", "Reported hundreds of millions of dollars in revenue with a team of just 11 people."),
        ("Character.ai", "Popularized AI entertainment and companionship; users spend an average of 2 hours per session in-app."),
    ]
    x_start = Inches(6.4)
    y = Inches(1.3)
    w = Inches(6.2)
    for i, (title, desc) in enumerate(cards):
        yy = y + i * Inches(1.6)
        shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, x_start, yy, w, Inches(1.45))
        shape.fill.solid()
        shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(0xF7, 0xF7, 0xF7)
        shape.line.color.rgb = RGBColor(0xDD, 0xDD, 0xDD)
        shape.line.width = Pt(1)
        tf = shape.text_frame
        tf.word_wrap = True
        p = tf.paragraphs[0]
